title: Surjectivity and boundary kernel of Picard restriction
statement: Let $C$ be a smooth affine connected curve over an algebraically closed field $k$ [def-sc-curves], and let $c:C\hookrightarrow Z$ be a compactification [lem-sc-compactification] with $Z$ a smooth connected curve. Pullback of invertible modules [def-sc-invertible-module] gives a surjective homomorphism $r:\operatorname{Pic}(Z)\to\operatorname{Pic}(C)$ [def-sc-picard-group], and $\ker r=\langle[\mathcal O_Z(P)]:P\text{ a closed point of }Z\setminus C\rangle$. No degree-zero quotient or choice of boundary point is asserted.

source.place: Proof: first paragraph, restriction and boundary divisors

proof.text: Apply [lem-sc-divisor-class-curve] on C and its smooth connected compactification. Restriction of divisors forgets the coefficients of the boundary points. Extend any divisor on C by zero at the boundary to obtain a divisor upstairs. The divisor restriction is therefore surjective.

source.place: Proof: first paragraph, restriction and boundary divisors

proof.text: The dense open immersion identifies the two function fields. At each point of C it identifies local rings and hence valuations, so a principal divisor upstairs restricts to the principal divisor of the same rational function downstairs.

source.place: Proof: first paragraph, restriction and boundary divisors

proof.text: If D restricts to div_C(f), subtract div_Z(f); the difference is supported on the boundary. Every boundary divisor restricts to zero. Thus the induced map on divisor classes has kernel generated by the boundary point classes.

source.place: Proof: first paragraph, restriction and boundary divisors

proof.text: The divisor-class comparison sends D to O(D). Restricting that module gives O(D restricted to C): inside the common function field they impose precisely the same valuation inequalities at points of C. This identifies the divisor-class map with Scheme.Pic.mapHom c.i and the boundary point generators with Scheme.Pic.ofClosedPoint. Hence restriction on Picard groups is surjective with the displayed kernel.

lean.statement:
theorem Scheme.Hom.pic_restriction_exact
    {k : Type u} [Field k] [IsAlgClosed k] {C : Scheme.{u}}
    (f : C ⟶ Spec (.of k)) [IsConnectedCurve f] [Smooth f] [IsAffine C]
    (c : Compactification f) [IsConnectedCurve c.g]
    [hsm : SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 c.g] :
    Function.Surjective (Scheme.Pic.mapHom c.i) ∧
      (Scheme.Pic.mapHom c.i).ker = Subgroup.closure
        {L | ∃ P : closedPoints c.Z, P.val ∉ Set.range c.i.base ∧
          L = @Scheme.Pic.ofClosedPoint k _ c.Z ⟨c.g⟩ hsm P}
